courses.title: Applied Probability Concepts
courses.description: Statistical and probabilistic methods to better describe and understand variability and uncertainty in civil engineering problems.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Construction Productivity
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of project management and practices. Definition of Construction Productivity and study how to measure construction productivity and how it relates to other organizational functions. Lean construction and influential factors (i.e. human factors) related to productivity.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Construction Financial Management
courses.description: Fundamental theories and applied methods for financial management of construction companies. Construction accounting, cash flow analysis, financial planning and management, and risk analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Construction Risk Management
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 4131 Basic principles of construction risk management, as it relates to project budget, schedule, and managing job site safety risk. Introduction to qualitative and quantitative methods of assessing risks, with discussion on how to mitigate them.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Advanced Construction Project Management
courses.description: Overviews of various project management tasks for construction project. Learning the use of various commercially-available project management software systems for a real-life problem given on each assignment. On-line collaboration, value engineering, and document management systems, cost estimating systems, scheduling systems, and 4D CAD visualization systems. Project-based lecture.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Undergraduate course in project management or equivalent.

courses.title: Construction Project Delivery Methods
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 4191 Introduction and analysis of different project delivery methods used for the construction of various types of projects, including the baseline traditional design-bid-build method and alternative project delivery methods (such design-build, construction manager at risk, public-private partnerships, and integrated project delivery). The course addresses the risks entailed in various forms of project delivery methods, as well as describes the contractor evaluation techniques and contract types.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Construction Scheduling
courses.description: Fundamentals of methods and procedures used in planning and scheduling construction projects, trade sequencing, recourses allocations, leveling and cost curves, utilization of both manual computer network systems. Corequisite(s): CE 4120L .
courses.prerequisites: ETC 305, ETC 304, or CE 3140 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Construction Scheduling Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamentals of methods and procedures used in planning and scheduling construction projects, trade sequencing, recourses allocations, leveling and cost curves, utilization of both manual computer network systems. Corequisite(s): CE 4120 .
courses.prerequisites: ETC 305, ETC 304, or CE 3140 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Construction Contracts
courses.description: The basic principles and detailed review of design drawings and contract documents, including plans, specifications and agreements involved in the construction of facilities.
courses.prerequisites: ETC 305, ETC 304, or CE 3140 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Construction Project Management and Accounting
courses.description: The basic theory and techniques of project management and the general organizational structure of a contracting firm. Project engineer role in managing the legal, financial, budget, and personnel aspects of a construction project.
courses.prerequisites: ETC 305, ETC 304, or CE 3140 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Project Life Cycle and Sustainability
courses.description: Investigations into green building construction practices and sustainability including use of novel or recycled materials, energy management and efficiency, water use/re-use, and indoor air quality. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of civil/construction projects.
courses.prerequisites: CE 3101 or CE 3101L , senior standing.

courses.title: Virtual Design Construction and Management - BIM
courses.description: Fundamental principles of Building Information Modeling (BIM) as it applies to construction activities such as: 1) Construction sequence studies, 2) Clash detection between different disciplines, 3) Automated cost estimating by extracting material data from a 3-D BIM model. Corequisite(s): CE 4171L .
courses.prerequisites: ETC 304, ETC 305, CE 3140 , CE 3501L , or CE 305L; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Virtual Design Construction and Management - BIM Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamental principles of Building Information Modeling (BIM) as it applies to construction activities such as: 1) Construction sequence studies, 2) Clash detection between different disciplines, 3) Automated cost estimating by extracting material data from a 3-D BIM model. Corequisite(s): CE 4171 .
courses.prerequisites: ETC 304, ETC 305, CE 3140 , CE 3501L , or CE 305L; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Total Quality Management
courses.description: TFocuses on the essence, principles, and practices of total quality management (TQM) in the construction industry. Ideas and topics covered are: process focus; customer satisfaction; inspection policies; economics of quality; and quality function deployment (QFD).
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Underground Construction and Trenchless Technology
courses.description: Learning methods that can be applied to make deteriorating underground pipeline infrastructures more sustainable. Theory and practice of underground construction methods including trenchless construction. Types of equipment, roles of site personnel, engineering design, contractual issues, and safety.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Temporary Construction Structures
courses.description: The basic design and construction of temporary structures with applications to concrete vertical and horizontal formwork; shoring, scaffolding, foundation underpinning, temporary bridges/retaining walls, design of cofferdams, diaphragm/slurry walls, and construction dewatering. Construction safety associated with temporary structures is emphasized.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Undergraduate course in estimating or equivalent.

courses.title: Construction Leadership and Ethics
courses.description: Individual, organizational and process/structure leadership in project setting. Four-step leadership transformational model for project leaders. Project leadership tools and applications to motivation, conflict management, team building and delegation of risk.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: GIS Applications in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts and techniques of geographic information systems (GIS). GIS applications in transportation, environmental assessment, water resources management, geoenvironmental analyses and other areas in civil engineering.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Pavement Design and Construction
courses.description: Cross Listed as: CE 4451 Fundamental principles of structural pavement design and common design methods: AASHTO, Caltrans, Asphalt Institute and Portland Cement Association. Typical highway construction practices and activities. Laboratory testing of highway materials and quality assurance during construction are also discussed.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, undergraduate course in geotechnical engineering, and engineering materials or equivalent.

courses.title: Street Maintenance, Rehabilitation and Management
courses.description: Fundamental principles of pavement management and life cycle. Pavement condition surveys and non-destructive testing are also discussed. In addition, students are introduced to typical street maintenance strategies including preservation and recycling.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, undergraduate course in geotechnical engineering, and engineering materials or equivalent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Instructor Consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Project
courses.description: Individual and independent work based on the project proposal, plan and schedule approved by the Project Committee members and Graduate Program Coordinator. Regular meetings and discussions with advisor.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, good academic standing, advancement to candidacy, and completion of approved project proposal.

courses.title: Master’s Thesis
courses.description: Individual and independent research work based on the thesis proposal, plan and schedule approved the Project Committee members and Graduate Program Coordinator. Regular meetings and discussions with advisor.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing; good academic standing; advancement to candidacy; completion of approved project proposal.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Comprehensive examination to satisfy the culminating experience requirement of the Master of Science in Civil Engineering (MSCE) degree. May enroll after completing the required course work, and it may be taken up to two times.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, consent of instructor, and good standing.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
